chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Amr ibn Khalid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Jibra'il (peace be upon him) said: 'O Messenger of Allah! We do not enter a house that contains a picture of a human, nor a house in which one urinates, nor a house that contains a dog.'

key_terms.يُبَالُ فِيهِ: In which one urinates (place of urination)

ai.seo_question: Why do angels not enter houses with pictures or dogs?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the spiritual sensitivity of the home environment, linking angelic presence to the removal of specific impurities and decorative elements. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'Tazhib al-Makan' (purification of space), where physical cleanliness and the absence of distracting images facilitate divine grace and angelic visitation.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban Bin Usman, from Amro Bin Khalid, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! We (Angels) neither enter a house wherein is a picture of a human, nor a house which has been urinated in, nor a house in which is a dog’.
en.sarwar: 12. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from more than one person from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Amr ibn Khalid who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
Jibril, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, we do not enter a house in which picture of human beings exists or a house in which people urinate or a house in which a dog exists.’”
